questions.prompt: What does the burst of 4625 events across 78 distinct accounts indicate?
options: Password spraying -- one password tried against many accounts, staying under per-account lockout thresholds
questions.explanation: The distinction matters operationally: lockout policy defends against brute force but not against spraying, which never exceeds the threshold for any individual account.

questions.prompt: Why is Event ID 7045 still present after the Security log was cleared?
options: 7045 cannot be cleared by any account
It is written to the System log, which the attacker did not clear, and it requires no audit policy to be generated
It was forwarded to a SIEM before the clear
7045 is stored in the registry rather than a log
questions.explanation: Attackers overwhelmingly target the Security log, leaving System, Application, and the Operational channels intact -- which is why service installation remains visible.

questions.prompt: What does the 4720 followed by 4728 eight seconds later represent?
options: Account creation immediately followed by privileged group addition -- close to definitional hands-on-keyboard persistence
A failed account creation and retry
Group Policy applying a new user template
questions.explanation: The name was chosen to blend in, and the eight-second gap indicates a scripted or hands-on sequence rather than a normal provisioning workflow.

questions.prompt: What can this excerpt NOT tell you?
options: How the attacker reached 10.14.22.87, and what processes ran -- there is no Sysmon or 4688 data here, only authentication
questions.explanation: Authentication events establish who logged in from where, but without process telemetry nothing here shows what actually executed on the host.
